summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy (EF 20%), type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and coronary artery disease, was admitted for worsening shortness of breath, chest pressure described as 'an aquarium on my chest,' and a 15-pound weight gain over two days. He presented with signs of acute on chronic systolic heart failure, including elevated BNP (5,314), moderate pulmonary edema on chest X-ray, and pitting edema. He was treated with an IV furosemide drip, initially at 10 mg/hr and increased to 13 mg/hr due to inadequate urine output. His weight decreased from 139 kg to 131.9 kg, and symptoms improved. He was transitioned to oral torsemide 80 mg AM and 40 mg PM, with addition of hydralazine and isosorbide mononitrate. Metoprolol was changed to 200 mg daily. His kidney function remained stable with creatinine up to 1.9. He was discharged home with services, weighing 131.9 kg, breathing comfortably, and with a plan for cardiology follow-up, including restarting losartan.
